title: Replace a configured database provider deliberately
goal: Replace accumulated DbContext configuration before using an isolated test database; choose full registration removal, retained lifetimes or an options copy without retaining the original provider.

selectionNotes: Only a fresh isolated service collection with the demonstrated simple AddDbContext<TContext> registration; no production settings, OnConfiguring provider, custom aliases, factories, pooling or prebuilt internal service provider.
Configuration-only removal keeps Transient contexts and Singleton options in this example; full removal deliberately re-registers Scoped contexts/options before building a new container.

WithoutExtension and RemoveExtension are separate options operations; they preserve unrelated configuration and do not remove DI callbacks. Infrastructure helper uses public generic methods with the runtime provider-extension type through reflection, without naming unsupported Internal provider types; no trimming or NativeAOT route.
SQLite and InMemory CRUD both execute; InMemory accepts duplicate indexed values and cannot prove relational behavior. The EF10 comparison is not a ninth .NET10 foundation.

prerequisites: Finish all test-registration mutations before building a new container or resolving options/context services. Discard any previously built provider; removal does not mutate existing instances.
Copy all canonical files into separate standalone version directories and restore the exact packages with the pinned SDK. Retrieval is offline; initial dependency setup requires the packages.

The fixture creates only disposable in-memory databases. Keep the externally owned SQLite test connection open across scopes and dispose it after the service provider; the closed original stand-in is never opened. No credentials, external service or production connection is used.
stabilityLimitations: Stable API shape in GA-targeted guidance, measured on RC2 packages and SDK. No experimental API suppression required. Actual GA reconciliation remains outstanding.

evidence.scope: Four isolated full/configuration-only SQLite/InMemory replacements, descriptor and resolved lifetime checks, original callback/flags/connection exclusion, CRUD across scopes, SQLite unique-index failure versus InMemory acceptance; retained/mixed configuration controls. EF10 rebuilds fresh allowlisted options with actual InMemory writes/reads.

humanProof.scope: Automated isolated SQLite/InMemory execution covers these bounded provider/lifetime/CRUD claims. Windows x64 packaged native SQLite only; other providers/platforms, trimming/AOT and GA remain unverified.
